name: Cornish–Windsor Covered Bridge
facts: The 1866 Cornish–Windsor Covered Bridge, 449 feet long, was built by Bela Jenks Fletcher and James Frederick Tasker for $9,000, a sum equivalent to nearly $198,000 in 2025.
Until 2008, the Cornish–Windsor Covered Bridge held the title of longest standing covered bridge in the United States, a record it earned after the Smolen–Gulf Bridge opened.

Designated a National Historic Civil Engineering Landmark by the ASCE in 1970, the bridge’s Town lattice truss—patented by Ithiel Town in 1820—remains a rare example of 19th-century timber engineering.
